function.name: library_reserve_book
function.description: Reserves a book in the library if available. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

book_id.description: The id of the book to reserve.

branch_id.description: The id of the library branch to reserve from.

return_date.description: The date the book is to be returned (optional). Default is ''

function.name: library_search_book
function.description: Searches for a book in the library within the specified city. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

book_name.description: The name of the book to search for.

availability.description: If true, search for available copies. If false or omitted, search for any copy regardless of availability. Default is false

genre.description: The genre of the book to filter search (optional). Default is ''

message.reasoning:
User wants to search for a book "The Alchemist" in New York City libraries. We need to call library_search_book with book_name="The Alchemist", city="New York City". Probably we want to search for availability? They didn't specify availability. The default is false, so it will search for any copy regardless of availability. But maybe we want to find an available copy. The user just says "尋找一本書" which means "search for a book". It might be better to set availability=true to find an available copy. But the default is false. The user didn't specify they want only available copies. So we can use default. But maybe it's safer to set availability=true. Let's interpret "尋找一本書" as searching for any copy. We'll set availability=false.

We also could ask clarifying question about whether they want an available copy. But let's proceed with a search.
